description: ICS Village brings together operators, researchers, and government leaders to address critical infrastructure defense, secure PLC coding, OT cloud exploitation, smart meter security, and ransomware resilience.

talks.title: Protecting Critical Infrastructure from Ransomware
talks.teaser: Cybersecurity leaders analyze the Colonial Pipeline and JBS ransomware attacks, debating mandatory reporting and defensive resilience for critical infrastructure.
talks.summary:
Ransomware Threats to National Infrastructure

High-profile ransomware intrusions against the Colonial Pipeline and JBS Foods underscored the catastrophic societal impacts of cyber extortion targeting industrial supply chains.

Bridging the IT/OT Operational Divide

Panelists discuss how administrative IT ransomware infections lead operators to proactively shut down operational technology (OT) pipelines out of precaution.

Evaluating Policy Mandates and Incident Reporting

The panel examines federal policy responses, including TSA pipeline security directives and mandatory incident reporting requirements for critical infrastructure operators.

Practical Strategies for Industrial Resiliency

Experts outline actionable defense blueprints, emphasizing immutable backups, network segmentation, and out-of-band manual override capabilities.

talks.title: Collaborative Cyber Defense & Enhanced Threat Intel
talks.teaser: Lauren Zabierek proposes a redesigned national cyber defense posture leveraging integrated public-private threat intelligence sharing networks.
talks.summary:
The Imperative for Public-Private Intelligence Sharing

Recent systemic supply chain intrusions and ransomware waves demonstrate that isolated enterprise defense cannot withstand coordinated nation-state campaigns.

Designing Integrated Cyber Defense Networks

Lauren Zabierek explores frameworks for real-time bidirectional intelligence sharing between government security agencies and private critical infrastructure operators.

Overcoming Legal, Technical, and Cultural Hurdles

The presentation examines barriers to effective information sharing—including classification hurdles, liability concerns, and automated telemetry standards.

Operationalizing Collaborative Defense

Zabierek presents actionable models for regional cyber defense collectives to pool defensive capabilities and accelerate threat hunting.

talks.title: Top 20 Secure PLC Coding Practices
talks.teaser: Sara Fluchs and Vivek Ponnada introduce the community-driven Top 20 Secure PLC Coding Practices, bringing secure engineering directly into ladder logic.
talks.summary:
Securing Programmable Logic Controllers at the Code Level

While perimeter firewalls and network monitoring are common in OT, the ladder logic running directly inside Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs) often lacks basic security checks.

Introducing the Top 20 Secure PLC Coding Practices

Sara Fluchs and Vivek Ponnada introduce an open-source, vendor-agnostic standard providing engineers with 20 actionable secure coding rules for PLC logic.

Defensive Engineering Inside Controller Logic

Key practices include monitoring PLC cycle times, validating analog sensor input ranges, and implementing software plausibility checks to detect sensor tampering.

Adopting Secure Coding in Industrial Automation

The authors provide integration blueprints for automation engineers, system integrators, and asset owners to embed secure coding into commissioning standards.

talks.title: Smart Meters: I'm Hacking Infrastructure and So Should You
talks.teaser: Hash Saehi dissects the hardware and RF protocols of electrical smart meters, demonstrating why auditing grid edge devices is vital for infrastructure resilience.
talks.summary:
The Strategic Importance of Smart Meter Security

Electrical smart meters form the critical edge interface of modern smart power grids, managing automated billing, load balancing, and remote power disconnects.

Hardware Teardown and Optical/RF Interface Auditing

Hash Saehi inspects commercial smart meter hardware, dumping firmware via SPI flash chips and reverse engineering ANSI optical communication ports.

Analyzing Grid Disconnect and Spoofing Vectors

In the wake of grid failures like the 2021 Texas freeze, Saehi demonstrates the potential for systemic load disruption if remote disconnect commands are abused.

Recommendations for Utilities and Meter Manufacturers

The author advocates for open vulnerability disclosure across utility hardware and urges manufacturers to enforce cryptographic firmware signing.

talks.title: Scripts and Tools to Help Your ICS InfoSec Journey
talks.teaser: Cutaway Security founder Don C. Weber reviews open-source tools and custom scripts to safely assess and gather telemetry from live industrial control networks.
talks.summary:
Navigating the Unique Constraints of ICS Security Assessments

Performing security assessments in industrial control environments requires specialized tools and cautious methodologies to prevent disrupting live physical processes.

Curating Open-Source ICS Discovery and Auditing Scripts

Don C. Weber presents a collection of purpose-built scripts and open-source tools developed by Cutaway Security for passive and active OT network analysis.

Safely Interrogating Industrial Protocols

Weber demonstrates utilizing custom Python scripts to poll Modbus, EtherNet/IP, and DNP3 devices without triggering controller fault states or buffer overruns.

A Practical Roadmap for Aspiring OT Security Analysts

The presentation provides guidance and lab setup recommendations for traditional IT security professionals transitioning into industrial cybersecurity.

talks.title: Network Traffic Analysis with Malcolm
talks.teaser: Seth Grove demonstrates Malcolm, an open-source network traffic analysis suite developed by INL and CISA for deep packet inspection of industrial protocols.
talks.summary:
Seth Grover, lead developer at Idaho National Laboratory, presents a comprehensive deep-dive into "Malcolm," an open-source network traffic analysis tool suite specifically tailored for operational technology (OT), industrial control systems (ICS), and enterprise IT networks.

[23:25] Grover walks through Malcolm's modular architecture, explaining how it integrates industry-standard open-source security tools into a cohesive Docker-based environment. The platform pairs Zeek for rich network protocol metadata generation with Suricata for signature-based intrusion detection, while leveraging Arkime (formerly Moloch) for full packet capture indexing and Elasticsearch/Kibana for visualization. Grover highlights Malcolm's native support for parsing proprietary and open industrial automation protocols, including Modbus, DNP3, CIP/EtherNet-IP, and BACnet.

[47:48] The presentation demonstrates Malcolm's automated log enrichment engine, which tags network sessions with NetBox asset inventory metadata, geo-IP coordinates, and threat intelligence feeds. Grover provides a live demonstration [01:12:32] exploring complex network captures, demonstrating how analysts can filter traffic over time histograms, identify anomalous ICS command sequences, trace encrypted SSL/TLS certificate anomalies, and conduct rapid forensic incident response within critical infrastructure environments.

(AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Living off the Land in an ICS/OT Penetration Test
talks.teaser: Aaron Boyd demonstrates Living off the Land (LotL) techniques in OT environments, utilizing native engineering tools and HMI scripts to pivot undetected.
talks.summary:
Evading Signature Detections with Living off the Land

Modern OT security appliances and application whitelisting solutions monitor for unknown binaries, forcing adversaries to rely on native tools already present on host systems.

Repurposing Native Engineering and HMI Utilities

Aaron Boyd demonstrates how attackers leverage built-in Windows administrative utilities, SCADA scripting engines, and vendor maintenance binaries for lateral movement.

Pivoting Across Industrial Control Segments

Using native PowerShell, WMI, and engineering workstation software, an operator can extract controller project files and send unauthorized PLC commands without dropping custom malware.

Defending Industrial Environments Against LotL Attacks

Boyd outlines behavioral monitoring strategies and strict execution policy configurations to detect malicious use of legitimate engineering utilities.

talks.title: Leveraging SBOMs to Enhance ICS Security
talks.teaser: Tom Pace explores leveraging Software Bills of Materials (SBOMs) to track third-party dependencies and supply chain risks in embedded ICS devices.
talks.summary:
The Supply Chain Blindspot in Industrial Control Systems

Industrial control devices often embed dozens of legacy third-party software libraries and firmware stacks (such as Ripple20 and Urgent/11) without asset owner visibility.

Understanding Software Bills of Materials (SBOMs)

Tom Pace reviews federal executive orders and NTIA guidance defining machine-readable SBOM formats (SPDX, CycloneDX) for tracking component dependencies.

Generating and Consuming SBOMs for Embedded Hardware

Pace demonstrates automated tools for generating SBOMs from firmware binaries and integrating them into enterprise vulnerability management platforms.

Operationalizing SBOMs for Rapid Vulnerability Triage

The author illustrates how asset owners can instantly determine whether newly disclosed zero-days affect their deployed operational technology fleets.

talks.title: ICS Village Keynote: Reading the Future with Useful Fiction
talks.teaser: Best-selling author and strategist P.W. Singer delivers the opening keynote for the DEF CON 29 ICS Village on useful fiction and forecasting cyber conflicts.
talks.summary:
Social Engineering and Human-Oriented Security

This presentation explores social engineering attacks and human vulnerability in security systems. Topics include psychological manipulation, pretexting, credential harvesting, and how attackers exploit human nature to bypass technical defenses.

(AI summary — Claude Haiku)

talks.title: Students Performing ICS Security Assessments
talks.teaser: Everett Community College students and faculty share experiences conducting mock security assessments on a custom 10-foot physical ICS training wall.
talks.summary:
Hands-On Industrial Cybersecurity Education

Everett Community College launched a groundbreaking 5-credit curriculum titled 'Assessing and Securing Control Systems' to train future critical infrastructure defenders.

Building a 10-Foot Physical ICS Training Wall

Dennis Skarr, Christopher Von Reybyton, and Alexander Vigovskiy showcase the custom-built training wall featuring real-world PLCs, HMIs, and simulated industrial processes.

Executing Student Capstone Security Audits

Students walk through their comprehensive capstone assessment, identifying network misconfigurations, unauthenticated Modbus commands, and weak HMI credentials.

Building Pathways into the Industrial Security Workforce

The presentation provides community colleges and universities with a blueprint for establishing hands-on OT cybersecurity training labs.

talks.title: ICS Village Opening and Introduction
talks.teaser: Organizers open the DEF CON 29 ICS Village, introducing scheduled talks, hands-on CTF challenges, interactive industrial walls, and training workshops.
talks.summary:
This talk covers industrial control systems security and critical infrastructure protection.

(AI summary — Claude Haiku)

talks.title: ICS Jeopardy
talks.teaser: Mary Brooks hosts an interactive round of ICS Jeopardy testing contestants on historical ICS incidents, nerdy fiction, and on-the-spot asset identification.
talks.summary:
Gamifying Industrial Cybersecurity Knowledge

Mary Brooks hosts an energetic, full-round game of Jeopardy tailored specifically for industrial control systems and cybersecurity professionals.

Categories in ICS Incidents and History

Contestants compete across categories spanning landmark cyber incidents (Stuxnet, BlackEnergy, Triton), industrial networking trivia, and nerd culture.

On-the-Spot Asset Identification Challenges

The game incorporates interactive speed rounds requiring participants to identify obscure industrial hardware, fieldbus cables, and PLC components.

Fostering Community Engagement and Education

The session blends technical education and entertainment to reinforce critical infrastructure cybersecurity concepts.

talks.title: ICS Intrusion Kill Chain Explained
talks.teaser: Javier Perez and Juan Escobar deconstruct the ICS Cyber Kill Chain, mapping adversary stages from initial IT ingress to OT process manipulation.
talks.summary:
The Distinct Dynamics of ICS Cyber Attacks

Unlike traditional IT data theft campaigns, cyber attacks against industrial control systems require deep familiarity with automated engineering processes and physical safety systems.

Deconstructing the Two-Stage ICS Cyber Kill Chain

Javier Perez and Juan Escobar examine the Michael Assante and Robert M. Lee ICS Kill Chain model, distinguishing Stage 1 (IT intrusion and preparation) from Stage 2 (OT execution and disruption).

Mapping Real-World Adversary Campaigns

The authors analyze historic campaigns (including Sandworm and Xenotime), illustrating how attackers establish beachheads, learn engineering workflows, and deploy destructive OT payloads.

Actionable Chokepoints for Incident Responders

Perez and Escobar identify key defensive detection chokepoints to intercept adversaries before they transition into Stage 2 execution.

talks.title: ICS CTI Information Sharing Between Brazil and the United States
talks.teaser: International defense experts discuss cross-border cyber threat intelligence sharing between the United States and Brazilian military Cyber Command.
talks.summary:
Cross-Border Cyber Defense for Critical Infrastructure

As industrial threats transcend national borders, bilateral threat intelligence sharing between allied nations is critical for early warning and collective defense.

The Brazilian Cyber Guardian Critical Infrastructure Exercise

Panelists review Brazil's annual Cyber Guardian national exercise, highlighting simulated attacks against power grids, financial networks, and water facilities.

Facilitating Bi-Directional US-Brazil Information Sharing

Leaders from US CISA, the Cyber Security Forum Initiative (CSFI), and Brazilian Cyber Command explore mechanisms to share actionable OT indicators of compromise.

Building Global Industrial Cybersecurity Partnerships

The panel outlines operational pathways for commercial asset owners and researchers to participate in international threat-sharing coalitions.

talks.title: Highlighting the Importance of Detection Context
talks.teaser: Otis Alexander analyzes the MITRE ATT&CK Evaluations for ICS, demonstrating why detection context and operational telemetry are vital for industrial defense.
talks.summary:
In this presentation at the DEF CON 29 ICS Village, Otis Alexander, cybersecurity engineer at MITRE, explores the vital importance of contextual correlation in industrial control system detection engineering. He begins at 03:00 by recounting a simulated adversarial attack against a mock gas facility, where operators manipulated valve states to induce a dangerous flammable gas release without triggering physical safety alarms or tripping baseline network thresholds.

Otis reviews the MITRE ATT&CK for ICS evaluation methodology at 06:00, discussing how various commercial security platforms were scored across specific offensive techniques. He explains why isolated, atomic alerts fail SOC analysts at 09:00, arguing that detecting an individual anomalous command is meaningless without understanding surrounding engineering workflows.

Demonstrating cross-data-source correlation at 12:00, Otis shows how tying endpoint Windows security events directly to industrial network packet captures establishes a coherent timeline of attacker activity. At 15:00, he illustrates how linking host authentication logs with subsequent PLC setpoint changes builds a compelling detection narrative. He concludes at 21:00 by urging ICS defenders and detection engineers to develop enriched correlation rules that bridge the divide between IT telemetry and OT process reality. (AI summary — Gemini Flash)

talks.title: Fortifying ICS: Hardening and Testing
talks.teaser: Dieter Sarrazyn outlines practical methodologies for embedding cybersecurity requirements, system hardening, and acceptance testing into industrial upgrade projects.
talks.summary:
Integrating Security into Industrial Engineering Projects

Industrial control environments frequently undergo expansions, software upgrades, and hardware retrofits where cybersecurity is treated as an afterthought.

Defining Measurable Security Requirements

Dieter Sarrazyn presents structured frameworks for establishing cybersecurity baselines during the initial project procurement and specification phases.

Executing Practical Hardening on OT Assets

Sarrazyn details hardening steps for HMIs, engineering workstations, and network switches—including disabling unneeded services, closing default ports, and enforcing role-based access.

Factory and Site Acceptance Security Testing

The author provides test plans for conducting security verification during Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT) and Site Acceptance Testing (SAT) before production commissioning.

talks.title: Do We Really Want to Live in the Cyberpunk World?
talks.teaser: Meet Can Kilic evaluates emerging cyber-physical threats to human augmentations, brain-computer interfaces, and connected insulin pumps.
talks.summary:
The Convergence of Cyber-Physical and Biological Systems

Advancements in medical technology and bioengineering are bringing cyber-physical systems directly into the human body through connected pacemakers, insulin pumps, and neuro-implants.

Threat Modeling Human Augmentation Technologies

Meet Can Kilic examines the realistic attack vectors facing next-generation brain-computer interfaces and implanted medical devices.

The Societal and Physical Stakes of Compromised Implants

The author discusses the severe safety, privacy, and bodily autonomy implications when biometric devices and medical telemetry are connected to cloud networks.

Establishing Secure Engineering Paradigms for Bio-Devices

Kilic urges the security community and biomedical engineers to establish fail-safe cryptographic and physical safety standards for human-integrated technology.

talks.title: Detecting Attackers with State Estimation
talks.teaser: Stefan Stephenson-Moe presents physics-based state estimation techniques to detect Stuxnet-like sensor spoofing and false data injection in industrial controllers.
talks.summary:
The Threat of Sensor Spoofing in Sophisticated OT Malware

Advanced industrial malware (like Stuxnet) manipulates physical processes while forging normal sensor telemetry to keep human operators unaware of impending equipment damage.

Principles of Physics-Based State Estimation

Stefan Stephenson-Moe explains how mathematical state estimation models calculate expected physical system behaviors based on physical laws (such as thermodynamics and fluid dynamics).

Detecting False Data Injection Attacks

By comparing real-time sensor measurements against estimated physical states, anomaly detection algorithms identify discrepancies caused by manipulated sensor packets.

Implementing State Estimation on Modern PLCs

The author demonstrates practical implementations running on edge controllers, providing a resilient layer of physical process verification.

talks.title: Crippling the Grid: Examination of Dependencies & Cyber Vulns
talks.teaser: Joe Slowik explores systemic multi-tier dependencies in the electrical power grid, demonstrating how targeting auxiliary systems can trigger grid collapse.
talks.summary:
Looking Beyond Direct Substation and Generation Attacks

Traditional power grid cybersecurity focuses heavily on direct attacks against substation switchgear and generator controllers, which require high adversary sophistication.

Analyzing Hidden Interdependencies in Electric Utilities

Joe Slowik investigates indirect dependency chains—such as fuel supply logistics, telecommunication backhauls, water cooling, and market scheduling systems.

Modeling Cascading Failures and Systemic Grid Collapse

Slowik illustrates how low-complexity cyber intrusions against third-party auxiliary services can propagate through interconnections, inducing regional generation trips.

Building Resilient Multi-Tier Defensive Architectures

The author urges grid operators and regulators to perform comprehensive dependency mapping and decouple critical control loops from external services.

talks.title: Consider the Data Source: Building Resilient ICS Telemetry
talks.teaser: Dan Gunter challenges assumptions about ICS security data sources, showing how to cross-correlate process data, network packets, and host logs for true visibility.
talks.summary:
The Constraints of Industrial Monitoring Environments

Protecting industrial control systems requires balancing zero tolerance for operational downtime with limited compute resources on legacy controllers.

Evaluating the Limitations of Single Telemetry Sources

Dan Gunter analyzes common industrial data sources (network taps, host logs, PLC engineering logs), demonstrating how each source can be blinded or spoofed individually.

Cross-Correlating Process Data and Network Telemetry

By synthesizing network packet captures with actual physical process telemetry (SCADA historian logs), defenders achieve high-fidelity situational awareness.

Designing Resilient OT Detection Architectures

Gunter provides practical blueprints for deploying multi-source telemetry pipelines that resist adversary evasion and data tampering.

talks.title: Building an ICS Firing Range in Our Kitchen
talks.teaser: Nico Leidecker and Moritz Thomas share how they engineered a portable, physical ICS cyber firing range with real PLCs, HMIs, and bridge models in their kitchen.
talks.summary:
The Necessity of Realistic Hands-On ICS Training

Developing elite ICS offensive and defensive skills requires hands-on experience with physical hardware, but commercial industrial training testbeds are prohibitively expensive.

Engineering a Portable Physical Cyber Range

Nico Leidecker and Moritz Thomas detail constructing a modular ICS firing range featuring real PLCs, industrial network switches, and custom motorized bridge models.

Integrating Red and Blue Team Simulation Scenarios

The creators walk through simulated attack scenarios, including Modbus command injection, firmware tampering, and defensive monitoring with open-source tools.

Open-Source Hardware and Software Blueprints

The authors provide schematics, bill of materials, and configuration guides for researchers to build their own budget-friendly OT simulation testbeds.

talks.title: Beetlejuice: The Lessons We Should Have Learned
talks.teaser: Tim Yardley extracts 15 operational cybersecurity lessons from historical ICS failures and incident response engagements to transform industrial defense.
talks.summary:
Extracting Practical Wisdom from Historical Incidents

Despite decades of industrial cybersecurity research, critical infrastructure operators frequently repeat the same fundamental security mistakes.

15 Core Lessons from the Trenches of OT Security

Tim Yardley distills real-world incident response findings into 15 operational maxims covering network segmentation, password hygiene, and vendor remote access.

Transforming Cynicism into Actionable Defense

The presentation emphasizes practical cultural shifts between plant floor operators and IT security teams to implement sustainable security practices.

A Pragmatic Blueprint for ICS Security Maturity

Yardley outlines incremental, low-risk hardening steps that asset owners can implement immediately without disrupting industrial operations.

talks.title: Down: Exploiting Vulnerabilities in the OT Cloud
talks.teaser: Claroty researchers disclose critical vulnerabilities in CODESYS Automation Server and WAGO PLCs, executing top-down attacks from OT cloud to physical plants.
talks.summary:
The Rapid Rise of Cloud-Connected Industrial Automation

Automation vendors increasingly deploy cloud-based management platforms (such as CODESYS Automation Server) to monitor, configure, and update field PLCs over the internet.

Auditing Cloud-to-PLC Architecture

Sharon Brizinov and Uri Katz analyze the communication protocols and authentication handshakes connecting cloud management servers to local industrial controllers.

Top-Down and Bottom-Up Exploitation Chains

The researchers uncover critical zero-days in CODESYS Automation Server and WAGO PLCs, demonstrating how compromising the cloud grants remote code execution on connected field PLCs.

Securing Industrial Cloud Management Platforms

The authors share their coordinated disclosure findings and provide security baselines for cloud-managed operational technology.

talks.title: Attract, Develop, & Retain an ICS Workforce
talks.teaser: John Ellis and Julia Atkinson present data-driven strategies for recruiting, training, and retaining industrial control systems cybersecurity talent.
talks.summary:
The Critical Shortage in Industrial Cybersecurity Talent

Over 60% of critical infrastructure organizations report acute shortages of qualified cybersecurity professionals, leaving vital industrial assets exposed to risk.

Overcoming Recruitment and Skill Set Barriers

John Ellis and Julia Atkinson analyze the dual competency required for ICS security—combining IT cybersecurity expertise with industrial engineering fundamentals.

Developing Effective Training and Mentorship Pipelines

The authors showcase successful workforce development programs, cross-training initiatives for plant floor engineers, and rotational apprentice programs.

Retaining High-Performing Industrial Security Teams

The presentation provides enterprise leaders with practical retention frameworks, career progression paths, and strategies to build inclusive security cultures.
